lesson.label: 📖 Bài học chính
lesson.title: 1. Minimalist vs. Maximalist
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Sophie is helping her friend Ella move into a new flat. They’re carrying boxes up the stairs.*
lines: Careful with that one. It’s full of plants.
Another one? Ella, this is the fourth box of plants.
I know. I’m **a bit of a hoarder**. I keep everything.
**I can see that.** You’ve got more cushions than chairs.
They make the place feel **cosy**. I like having my favourite things **on display**: photos, books, **souvenirs** from my trips.
I get that. I’m **the complete opposite**. I’m a real **minimalist**. My flat’s almost empty: a sofa, a table, a bed, and **that’s about it**.
I know. Doesn’t it feel a bit cold?
Not to me. **Clutter** makes me feel stressed. When everything’s **neat and tidy**, I can actually relax. Plus, cleaning only takes ten minutes.
That’s the one thing I’m **jealous of**. **Dusting** all my shelves **takes forever**.
Last year, I **decluttered** my whole flat. I **gave away** half my clothes, and honestly, I don’t miss any of them.
I could never do that. I’m too **attached to** my things. Most of them have **sentimental value**. I still have concert tickets from 2015.
That’s the difference between us. You keep things for the memories. **I’d rather** keep the memories **than** the stuff.
**Fair point.** But **bare** white walls just make me sad.
So where’s all this going to go? Your new place isn’t very big, and there’s **hardly any storage space**.
I’ll **make it work**. A few more shelves, some hooks on the walls…
Or you could **get rid of** a few cushions. They **take up** a lot of **space**.

lesson.title: 2. Home, sweet home
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Ben and Hannah are colleagues. On Monday, Hannah asks Ben about the flat he moved into at the weekend.*
lines: How’s the new place? You moved last weekend, didn’t you?
Yeah. It’s only **a studio**, and it’s a bit small, but **it’s all mine**. It’s **fully furnished**, so I didn’t need to buy much.
Nice. How does it feel to **live alone** after sharing a house for so long?
Amazing. I lived with four **flatmates** for three years. I had to wait twenty minutes for the bathroom every morning, and we always argued about **whose turn it was to take out the bins**.
Exactly. It was fun sometimes, but now I finally **have the place to myself**.
Isn’t it a bit lonely, though?
Sometimes, in the evenings. But I’m enjoying **the peace and quiet**, and I **invite friends over** more often now.
What about **the rent**? I bet it’s not cheap.
Before, we **split the bills** five ways. Now **the bills are all on me**.

That’s why I’m thinking of **moving back in with** my parents for a year. I’d **lose some of my freedom**, and my mum would ask where I’m going every time I leave the house. But I could **save for a deposit**.
Yeah, renting is so expensive. My old landlord **put** the rent **up** twice last year. By the way, are you looking at flats or houses?
Flats, probably. A house with a garden would be lovely, but I **can’t afford** one in the city centre. Houses are cheaper in **the suburbs**, but **the commute** would be awful.
Well, if you ever need a break from your parents, you’re welcome to **crash on my sofa**.

homework.title: Part 2: Listening
homework.intro: Listen to Laura talking about a big change in her life, then answer the questions.
homework.podcast: 🎧 My home: from a big house to a tiny flat

script.text: Hi, I'm Laura, and today I want to talk about the biggest change I've made in my life: moving into a tiny flat.

Two years ago, I lived in a big house in the suburbs with my husband and our two cats. It had four bedrooms and a garden. It sounds perfect, right? But ==the commute to the city took over an hour each way, and we spent every weekend cleaning and fixing things.==

So we decided to sell the house and rent a small flat near my office. The problem was, the flat only had one bedroom. ==We had to get rid of more than half of our things. That was really hard== for my husband, because he's a bit of a hoarder. He kept saying, =="But I might need this one day!"==

In the end, we gave away most of our furniture to friends and family. The only big thing we kept was ==my grandmother's old piano==. It takes up a lot of space, but it has ==too much sentimental value== to sell.

Now, I walk to work in ten minutes, and cleaning the whole flat takes less than an hour. Do I miss anything? Honestly, ==I miss the garden==, especially in summer. But I don't miss spending my weekends looking after a big house.
My advice? ==Before you buy something new, ask yourself: do I really need it, or do I just want it?==

questions.q: Why did Laura and her husband decide to move?
options: Their house was too expensive to rent.
They spent too much time travelling and looking after the house.
questions.why: “The commute to the city took over an hour each way, and we spent every weekend cleaning and fixing things.”

questions.q: What was the most difficult part of moving?
options: Finding a flat near Laura’s office
Reducing the number of things they owned
questions.why: “We had to get rid of more than half of our things. That was really hard…”

questions.q: How did Laura’s husband feel about getting rid of things?
options: He worried that he might need them later.
He wanted to sell them online.
questions.why: “He kept saying, ‘But I might need this one day!’”

questions.q: Why did they keep the piano?
questions.why: It was her grandmother’s piano and “has too much sentimental value to sell.”

questions.q: What does Laura miss most about the house?

options: Think carefully before you buy things.
Always rent instead of buying a home.
Try to live close to where you work.
questions.why: “Before you buy something new, ask yourself: do I really need it, or do I just want it?”
